threat_recommendations.title: Sweep balance consent
threat_recommendations.original_threat: Opening/selecting a payment discloses its one-time address to an RPC provider.
threat_recommendations.current_behavior: Opening Sweep, changing rows and changing inputs do not initiate a balance read. Every balance refresh needs a disclosed click; stale session/selection/RPC results are invalidated, including the async client-acquisition boundary.
threat_recommendations.remaining_work: Run actual combined-source browser journeys and rapid-switch/lock behavior in the intended browser configuration.
threat_recommendations.residual_limitations: A deliberate read and a later sweep still expose the address, request timing and connecting IP. Already-sent requests cannot be recalled.

threat_recommendations.title: Provider exposure notices
threat_recommendations.original_threat: Users do not know which scan/export/sweep activity identifies their payments to a provider.
threat_recommendations.current_behavior: Pages scan/sweep and recovery-export views contain per-flow notices. The obsolete automatic-balance wording was corrected. The fresh threat-model ledger replaces stale all-library/not-implemented claims.
threat_recommendations.remaining_work: Review full-profile notices separately, keep older audit/matrix claims historical, and perform native-language/accessibility acceptance.
threat_recommendations.residual_limitations: A disclosure establishes informed action, not provider confidentiality. Critical unreviewed translations intentionally use English.

threat_recommendations.title: RPC metadata controls
threat_recommendations.original_threat: Ambient cookies, referrers or HTTP cache increase unintended metadata retention.
threat_recommendations.current_behavior: The shared fetch transport sets credentials omit, no-referrer, no-store and redirect error. #220 and #222 overlap was resolved without dropping the POST regression.
threat_recommendations.remaining_work: Complete final dependency-aligned combined tests and built-browser verification.
threat_recommendations.residual_limitations: These flags do not hide IP, target origin, RPC method/body or provider logs; browser/extension compromise remains outside this control.

threat_recommendations.title: Secret-bearing endpoint storage
threat_recommendations.original_threat: Provider API credentials embedded in endpoint paths/queries persist in plaintext browser preferences.
threat_recommendations.current_behavior: Settings flags likely path/query secrets and offers session-only RPC endpoints held in module memory. Persisted settings omit an exact endpoint selected for session-only storage.
threat_recommendations.remaining_work: Actual browser storage-denial/reload acceptance and clear user guidance for existing saved endpoints.
threat_recommendations.residual_limitations: Detection is heuristic; saved non-session URLs remain plaintext. Memory-only endpoints are still visible to a compromised active page.

threat_recommendations.title: Tight hosting egress policy
threat_recommendations.original_threat: A broad connect-src permits more exfiltration destinations if script execution is compromised.
threat_recommendations.current_behavior: Build-time GHOSTPAY_CONNECT_ORIGINS support, CSP/artifact checks, declared-origin guards and hosting guidance exist. Generic csp.mjs builds still use self/https/wss if no allowlist is configured.
threat_recommendations.remaining_work: Qualify final release artifacts with the approved dedicated origin and exact allowlist, then inspect actual served policy. GitHub Pages does not apply a custom _headers file.
threat_recommendations.residual_limitations: CSP is one layer and does not protect against an origin/host that serves changed code; user-added endpoints may be blocked by a tight build.

threat_recommendations.title: Honest Tor boundary
threat_recommendations.original_threat: An onion-hosted bundle is mistaken for Tor-routed RPC or payment anonymity.
threat_recommendations.current_behavior: Tor guidance separates bundle hosting, browser routing and independent RPC/wallet traffic and retains UNTESTED status. Settings exposes the acknowledged network selection. This documentation refresh corrects the older deploy/TOR.md statement denying that control and records the plain-HTTP loopback CSP limit.
threat_recommendations.remaining_work: Execute real Tor bootstrap/reachability/browser/provider tests and record their versions, source and traffic boundary. Plain-HTTP loopback compatibility remains constrained by the shipped CSP.
threat_recommendations.residual_limitations: The browser page cannot verify Tor routing; the provider still sees request content; wallet-extension traffic is outside app control.

threat_recommendations.title: Destination reuse without plaintext linkage
threat_recommendations.original_threat: Repeated or known-wallet sweep destinations link payments; persisting the warning history can create an extra local linkage record.
threat_recommendations.current_behavior: Classifier warnings are wired into Sweep. The address-link ledger is in memory, reset on lock/session changes, protected by epochs against late results, and copied on read. The legacy plaintext key is deleted best effort and never imported.
threat_recommendations.remaining_work: Final combined qualification and actual browser lock/reload/session acceptance.
threat_recommendations.residual_limitations: Warnings cover only the active session and are advisory. Earlier sessions/devices are not checked; denied storage can retain ignored legacy bytes.

threat_recommendations.title: Private v4 checkpoint names
threat_recommendations.original_threat: Public meta-address keys allow an observer of browser storage to test which seller was scanned.
threat_recommendations.current_behavior: Private HKDF-SHA256 v4 names use the correct loaded viewing key, chain and key identifier. Key lending/caches are session-bound. v1/v2 and both conflicting v3 formats are ignored and purged best effort; rescan is intentional.
threat_recommendations.remaining_work: Combined restart, storage denial, multi-tab and reorg browser acceptance; retain the rescan/migration disclosure.
threat_recommendations.residual_limitations: Cursor contents remain plaintext/unauthenticated; opaque identifiers and block progress still reveal use. Public reconciliation/key-vault headers are a separate residual.

threat_recommendations.title: Minimal receipts
threat_recommendations.original_threat: A receipt unnecessarily adds the one-time address and increases linkability to the seller signer.
threat_recommendations.current_behavior: Receipt payload omits stealthAddress by default. An explicit checkbox is required to include it; both forms remain signed and bound to invoice/payment facts. #233 retains signature/tamper assertions in browser fixtures.
threat_recommendations.remaining_work: Repeat the actual #233 Pages/browser journey at the final combined candidate. E9 proves upstream browser execution only; collection/component tests are not substitutes.
threat_recommendations.residual_limitations: Transaction hash, chain, amount, invoice digest and stable signer still allow public-chain and peer linkage.

threat_recommendations.title: Invoice confidentiality and identity rotation
threat_recommendations.original_threat: Plaintext invoice details and stable identity keys correlate invoices.
threat_recommendations.current_behavior: CreateInvoice defaults to encryption. The standard bearer link contains its key; passphrase mode is separate. Pay checks signatures and displays optional pinned-signer trust. Per-invoice signer selection is not implemented in the Pages creation flow.
threat_recommendations.remaining_work: Design and qualify per-invoice signer behavior if required, including trust/receipt compatibility. Run real encrypted-invoice and tamper browser acceptance.
threat_recommendations.residual_limitations: Bearer-link holders can decrypt private details; public amount/chain and stable meta-address remain linkable. #234 does not force Pay UI to reject every unpinned signer.

threat_recommendations.title: Relayer traffic and retention
threat_recommendations.original_threat: Quote and sweep reveal and correlate owner, destination, amount, IP and timing.
threat_recommendations.current_behavior: Web requests use fixed-size padding buckets; compatible server validation/ingress configuration and retention documentation exist. A specific old-server refusal permits one unpadded retry. Signed quote tuples remain part of the protocol.
threat_recommendations.remaining_work: Separate optional-relayer compatibility and actual ingress qualification; a quote-less design needs fee/signature/protocol work. No hosted service is required by Pages.
threat_recommendations.residual_limitations: Padding changes request size only. Operator/proxy/RPC retention and quote correlation remain. Real Tor ingress was not executed.

threat_recommendations.title: Bulk receipt evidence
threat_recommendations.original_threat: Per-match receipt reads identify which announcements belong to the seller.
threat_recommendations.current_behavior: An optional cap up to 500 fetches router evidence for selected page transactions before local matching. Abort propagation now stops scheduling additional requests and invalidates late work; scanClient regression was independently rerun.
threat_recommendations.remaining_work: Measure complete RPC traces for covered/overflow/non-router pages and adversarial providers. Decide/document acceptable traffic cost and defaults rather than claiming general unlinkability.
threat_recommendations.residual_limitations: Off by default. Bounds, fallback, other calls, second providers, timing and request volume limit privacy; already-dispatched requests remain observable.

threat_recommendations.title: Non-EVM match privacy
threat_recommendations.original_threat: Outspend and per-match balance requests reveal matched BTC/Solana/Tron addresses.
threat_recommendations.current_behavior: Retained full-profile source moves Solana/Tron balance reads to sweep. Bitcoin has local spend evidence with a provider fallback for unknown state; #219 consent/worker/header work remains separately valuable.
threat_recommendations.remaining_work: Consolidate #219 consent/worker/header semantics and separately qualify each experimental chain with external fixtures; do not enable those routes to finish the Pages beta.
threat_recommendations.residual_limitations: Unknown spend state and signing can still require address/outpoint queries. None of these full-profile paths is certified by the Pages local results.

threat_recommendations.title: Network selection and own-node enforcement
threat_recommendations.original_threat: A profile label may imply private routing while cached clients still reach a third-party provider.
threat_recommendations.current_behavior: Acknowledged per-purpose direct/Tor Browser selection and own-node policy are exposed in Settings. createSelectedRpc enforces allowed own-node targets before construction and every dispatch/retry; no direct fallback on policy refusal.
threat_recommendations.remaining_work: Real Tor/OHTTP/own-node/browser acceptance is absent; profile provenance and all request-purpose boundaries need independent network verification.
threat_recommendations.residual_limitations: Tor Browser mode still uses ambient fetch and cannot prove routing. Endpoint syntax is not ownership proof; already-sent requests cannot be withdrawn. The validator permits plain-http loopback scan proxies, but the shipped CSP blocks them and the build allowlist parser excludes http; this compatibility gap remains open.

threat_recommendations.title: Padded scan ranges and PIR research
threat_recommendations.original_threat: Precise range boundaries expose start/progress and activity correlation.
threat_recommendations.current_behavior: padBlocks is wired through scan-source.padRange and the fixed-window decorator with validated caps and head/grid bounds; default extra padding is zero. Active scan source choices are RPC and indexer, not PIR.
threat_recommendations.remaining_work: Qualify real-provider request counts/bounds and separately review any future experimental PIR integration. Do not label existing library code a shipped toggle.
threat_recommendations.residual_limitations: Padding costs additional requests and does not hide IP, overall scan volume, timing or follow-on address/transaction queries.
